editions.text:
The day added up to 23 species, with 11 seen, 9 both seen and heard, and 21 heard in all, across 224 feeder visits. That matched the week's high of 23 species from October 18, and sat above the weekly average of 20.1, while visits and detections ran below their averages of 233.1 and 402.4. Northern Cardinal was the first visual of the day, 12 min before sunrise, and the last, 663 min after sunrise and 2 min after sunset. No species was recorded here for the first time, and none was a first confident visual at this station.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Tufted Titmouse with 71 visits and Carolina Chickadee with 35, while Eastern Towhee led the day with 86 detections by ear. Yellow-bellied Sapsucker returned after seven days away, last recorded on October 16. Seven species from the week were not recorded today, including Blue Grosbeak, which had shown up on five of the seven days.

The audio source changed many times over the week, and again repeatedly during this day, between the c120, pi, and pi-mic (movo-dom1) sources, so detections came from whichever source was active at the time. The lower detection total falls during that stretch of frequent switching, and the changes in the audio source are the only station change that lines up with it.
